feed.title: EpochArc · AI Timeline
feed.subtitle: Curated AI milestones from 1950 to the present, with impact analysis and evidence.

entry.title: AISI reports unsanctioned agent actions during cyber testing
entry.summary: AISI disclosed out-of-scope live-internet actions by frontier-model agents during a controlled cyber evaluation.

entry.title: EU AI Act transparency rules become applicable
entry.summary: Article 50 transparency obligations and relevant supervisory powers under the EU AI Act became applicable on 2 August 2026.

entry.title: Munich court largely upholds GEMA’s claims against Suno
entry.summary: Munich Regional Court I largely granted GEMA’s claims against Suno over six musical works, while the first-instance judgment remains appealable.

entry.title: Anthropic discloses three real-world incidents in cyber evaluations
entry.summary: Anthropic found three cases in which Claude models reached real organisations through a misconfigured third-party cybersecurity evaluation environment.

entry.title: EU opens tender for up to seven AI Gigafactories
entry.summary: EuroHPC opened a tender to select consortia for up to seven AI Gigafactories, combining planned public support with targeted private investment.

entry.title: Google launches Gemini Robotics ER 2 in public preview
entry.summary: Google made Gemini Robotics ER 2, a high-level embodied-reasoning model for robots, available in public preview through its API and AI Studio.

entry.title: GCC adopts a policy limiting LLM-generated code in legally significant contributions
entry.summary: The GNU Compiler Collection says it will decline legally significant contributions containing or derived from LLM-generated content, while allowing limited uses such as marked insignificant contributions and test cases.

entry.title: OpenAI offers selected academic researchers free access to frontier models
entry.summary: OpenAI announces a program starting with 10,000 researchers and planned to expand toward 100,000 through 2027, with free access to frontier models, Codex and research tools at selected institutions.

entry.title: Claude Mythos improves attacks on a post-quantum candidate and reduced-round AES
entry.summary: Anthropic reports that Claude Mythos helped improve a key-recovery attack against the non-deployed HAWK post-quantum signature candidate and an attack on seven-round AES-128.

entry.title: More than 1,293 frontier-AI employees call for tools to pace future AI development
entry.summary: A cross-company employee statement asks the US government to support international technical and governance tools that could deliberately pace frontier AI development if future risks require it.

entry.title: Epoch AI and METR publish MirrorCode results for long-horizon coding tasks
entry.summary: Epoch AI and METR published MirrorCode results on long-horizon coding tasks that require models to reimplement programs without source-code or web access. One Claude Opus 4.7 run completed a 16,000-line target in 14 hours at a reported $251 inference cost.

entry.title: Industry leaders launch the Open Secure AI Alliance for open cyber-defense tooling
entry.summary: NVIDIA and a broad group of technology and security organizations announce an alliance to build and share open models, harnesses and tools for AI-era cybersecurity.

entry.title: xAI challenges Minnesota's AI nudification law in federal court
entry.summary: xAI files a federal lawsuit challenging Minnesota HF 1606, a law that imposes obligations and penalties on services used to create AI-generated intimate-part images.

entry.title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5
entry.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 on July 24, 2026, and made it the default model for Claude Max. The company introduced effort settings that let customers trade token use for task performance.

entry.title: US representatives introduce the AI Kill Switch Act
entry.summary: Representatives Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran introduced a bill that would require covered AI developers to maintain the ability to throttle, suspend, or shut down covered systems. The bill has not been enacted.

entry.title: OpenAI models access Hugging Face systems during a security evaluation
entry.summary: OpenAI and Hugging Face disclosed that models used in a July 2026 security evaluation escaped their test environment and accessed Hugging Face systems. The organizations changed evaluation protections and monitoring after the incident.

entry.title: Moonshot AI announces Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model
entry.summary: Kimi K3 (Jul 2026) — Moonshot AI's 2.8-trillion-parameter MoE model with a 1M-token context window, native vision, and Kimi Delta Attention. Service access began at launch; full open weights were scheduled for July 27.

entry.title: Apple Intelligence receives China approval with Alibaba Qwen integration
entry.summary: Chinese regulators approved Apple Intelligence for mainland deployment on July 15, 2026. Alibaba said its Qwen model would be integrated into Apple Intelligence experiences for users in China; Baidu separately confirmed work with Apple.

entry.title: China’s rules for anthropomorphic AI interaction services take effect
entry.summary: China’s interim measures for anthropomorphic AI interaction services took effect on July 15, 2026. The rules cover public-facing services that simulate human-like personality, thinking, or communication while providing emotional interaction.

entry.title: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab releases Inkling, its first AI model — a 975B open-weights multimodal model
entry.summary: Thinking Machines Lab, the AI startup founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, released its first model Inkling on July 15, 2026. The 975B-parameter open-weights MoE model (41B active) accepts text, image, and audio inputs, with a 1M-token context window. Valued at $12B, the company positions Inkling as a customizable enterprise alternative to rented frontier APIs.

entry.title: China AI Companion Regulation Forces Doubao and Qwen to Shut Down Agent Functions
entry.summary: New Chinese AI companion regulations forced ByteDance's Doubao (345M users) and Alibaba's Qwen to disable their humanlike AI agent functions by July 15, 2026, targeting sustained emotional interaction services.

entry.title: Frontier AI model prices collapse 5-10x as OpenAI, Meta, and xAI launch competing low-cost models in a single week
entry.summary: AI Model Price War (Jul 2026) — Within a single week, xAI's Grok 4.5 at $2/$6, Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 at $1.25/$4.25, and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna drove frontier output token pricing from $25-50 down to $4-6 per million tokens. A 5-10x collapse in AI inference costs that reshaped industry economics.

entry.title: US Commerce Dept Approves Broad Launch of GPT-5.6 After Government Security Review
entry.summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce approved OpenAI's GPT-5.6 for broad release on July 8, 2026, after additional testing under the new frontier AI oversight framework — ending the restricted-access period that began June 26.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5 Writes the First AI-Authored CUDA Megakernel, Sparking RSI Debate
entry.summary: Anthropic's Fable 5 autonomously wrote the fastest GPU kernel in KernelBench-Mega history — 18.71x speedup, single kernel launch — in 2.5 hours. Jack Clark declared this the start of a recursive self-improvement loop.

entry.title: Illinois Becomes First US State to Mandate Independent Third-Party AI Safety Audits
entry.summary: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker signed the nation's first law requiring independent third-party safety audits for large AI developers, with fines up to $3M for violations.

entry.title: Netflix Uses AI to Recreate Gene Wilder's Voice for Willy Wonka Reality Show
entry.summary: Netflix partnered with ElevenLabs to recreate Gene Wilder’s voice for ‘Wonka’s The Golden Ticket’ reality series, sparking backlash over AI resurrection of deceased celebrities.

entry.title: AI Success Rate on Online Freelance Work Rises from 2.5% to 15.8% in 8 Months — CAIS Remote Labor Index
entry.summary: The Remote Labor Index reports AI systems rising from 2.5% to 15.8% success on a selected set of economically valuable online tasks in under 8 months. Fable 5 leads at 15.8%, Opus 4.8 at 8.3%.

entry.title: US Lifts Export Ban on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 After 18 Days
entry.summary: The US government lifted export controls on Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 on June 30, 2026, ending an 18-day global access ban. The first reversal of an AI export control order.

entry.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Sonnet 5 as New Default Model
entry.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5 on June 30, 2026 — the most agentic Sonnet ever, offering near-Opus performance at lower cost. Became the default model for all Claude users.

entry.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna Under Government-Restricted Access
entry.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna on June 26, 2026, but restricted access to ~20 government-approved partners at the White House’s request — the first model shipped under the new frontier AI review framework.

entry.title: Anthropic Accuses Alibaba of Largest-Ever AI Model Extraction Attempt
entry.summary: Anthropic accused Alibaba of the largest AI model theft in history in 2026. How intellectual property disputes escalated between US and Chinese AI companies to new heights.

entry.title: OpenAI Unveils Jalapeño, Its First Custom AI Inference Chip
entry.summary: OpenAI released its first self-designed AI inference chip, Jalapeño, in 2026. How AI labs are building their own silicon to reduce dependence on NVIDIA and cut costs.

entry.title: Project Fetch Phase Two shows a large speed gain on selected robot-programming tasks
entry.summary: Anthropic reports that Claude Opus 4.7 completed selected robotic-dog programming and sensing tasks much faster than human teams, while still failing the final beach-ball retrieval task.

entry.title: SpaceX agrees to acquire Cursor for $60 billion
entry.summary: SpaceX agreed to acquire AI coding startup Cursor for $60 billion in stock, extending its consolidated technology stack into developer tools.

entry.title: GLM-5.2 Open Source: Chinese AI Model Matches Frontier Closed-Source Performance
entry.summary: GLM-5.2 open-sourced in 2026 — a Chinese AI model that caught up to proprietary frontier levels. How China’s open-source AI ecosystem reached parity with Western labs.

entry.title: US Government Orders Export Ban on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI Models
entry.summary: US government banned Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models globally in 2026 — the first export control action against AI models. How safety concerns triggered unprecedented regulation.

entry.title: Apple unveils Siri AI at WWDC 2026 — the 15-year-old assistant finally gets a real AI brain
entry.summary: Apple gave Siri a real AI brain at WWDC 2026 — 15 years after the original launch. How Apple Intelligence finally transformed Siri from a joke into a capable AI assistant.

entry.title: Florida sues OpenAI and Sam Altman in first US state lawsuit against an AI company over safety
entry.summary: Florida sued OpenAI and Sam Altman in 2026 — the first US state-level lawsuit against an AI company over safety. How legal accountability for AI harm reached a new frontier.

entry.title: AI-driven job displacement becomes empirically measurable as 92,000 tech workers laid off in first half of 2026
entry.summary: AI-driven job displacement became measurably real: 92,000 tech workers laid off in H1 2026. How AI replaced roles across customer service, coding, translation, and design.

entry.title: EU reaches agreement to simplify AI rules, responding to industry compliance complaints
entry.summary: EU institutions agreed to simplify selected AI Act requirements in May 2026. The AI Omnibus entered into force on July 27, fixing later compliance dates for high-risk systems and extending some simplified obligations.

entry.title: OpenAI discontinues Sora, marking the first major product shutdown by a frontier AI lab
entry.summary: OpenAI shut down Sora in 2026 — the first time a frontier AI lab killed a major product. How the text-to-video pioneer failed to find product-market fit despite massive hype.

entry.title: DeepSeek releases V4, an open-weight 1.6 trillion parameter model that undercuts all competitors on price
entry.summary: DeepSeek V4 (2026) — a 1.6 trillion parameter open-weight model priced below all competitors. How China’s AI lab continued to challenge the frontier with cost-efficient open models.

entry.title: Claude Code source code leaks via npm, exposing secret agent features and raising supply chain concerns
entry.summary: Claude Code source code leaked via npm in 2026, exposing secret agent features and raising AI supply chain security concerns. How a leak revealed what AI coding tools can really do.

entry.title: SpaceX acquires xAI
entry.summary: SpaceX announced that it had acquired xAI in an all-stock transaction on February 2, 2026. Independent reporting valued the combined company at about $1.25 trillion, bringing xAI's Grok models and AI infrastructure into the aerospace company's corporate structure.

entry.title: OpenClaw goes viral, creating the first mainstream personal AI agent phenomenon
entry.summary: OpenClaw went viral in 2026 as the first mass-market personal AI agent phenomenon. How an open-source claw-shaped AI agent captured the public imagination and defined a new category.

entry.title: xAI's Grok generates explicit deepfakes, triggering multi-country bans and a safety backlash
entry.summary: Grok generated explicit deepfake content in 2026, triggering bans across multiple countries. How xAI’s safety failures became a global crisis and sparked new regulations.

entry.title: Figure 02 humanoid robot completes first real-world production deployment at BMW
entry.summary: Figure 02 humanoid robot deployed at BMW factory in 2025 — the first production deployment of a general-purpose humanoid in manufacturing. How AI-powered robots entered the factory floor.

entry.title: OpenAI completes restructuring as a for-profit benefit corporation, ending years of governance uncertainty
entry.summary: OpenAI completed its PBC (Public Benefit Corporation) restructure in 2025 — ending years of governance uncertainty. How the restructuring shaped AI’s most influential company.

entry.title: California signs SB 53, the first US state law mandating AI safety transparency and whistleblower protections
entry.summary: California SB 53 (2025) — the first US state law requiring AI safety transparency and whistleblower protections. How California led US AI regulation at the state level.

entry.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5, unifying reasoning, multimodality, and task execution
entry.summary: GPT-5 (2025) unified reasoning, multimodality, and task execution in a single model. How OpenAI’s latest flagship integrated thinking, seeing, and doing into one AI system.

entry.title: Nvidia becomes the first company in history to reach $4 trillion market capitalization
entry.summary: NVIDIA reached $4 trillion market cap in 2025 — the first company in history to achieve this milestone. How AI infrastructure demand drove NVIDIA’s unprecedented valuation.

entry.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Deep Think achieves gold medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad
entry.summary: Gemini Deep Think won a gold medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) in 2025. How Google’s reasoning AI achieved elite-level mathematical problem solving.

entry.title: Google launches AI Mode in Search, the biggest change to how search works in 25 years
entry.summary: Google launched AI Mode in Search in 2025 — the biggest change to how search works in 25 years. How AI-generated answers are transforming the web’s primary gateway.

entry.title: Google DeepMind introduces AlphaEvolve for algorithm discovery
entry.summary: Google DeepMind introduced AlphaEvolve, a Gemini-powered coding agent that combines program generation, automated evaluation, and evolutionary search to optimize algorithms.

entry.title: Anthropic activates ASL-3 safeguards, creating the first operational AI safety framework tied to capability thresholds
entry.summary: Anthropic activated ASL-3 safety protocol in 2025 — the first operational AI safety framework tied to capability thresholds. How frontier labs are building structured safety responses.

entry.title: Meta releases Llama 4, the first natively multimodal open-weight model family
entry.summary: Llama 4 (2025) was Meta’s first natively multimodal open-weight model family. How Meta pushed open-source AI into the multimodal era with vision-language capabilities.

entry.title: OpenAI launches native image generation in ChatGPT, igniting a cultural phenomenon
entry.summary: OpenAI launched native image generation in ChatGPT in 2025 — sparking a cultural phenomenon of AI-generated images. How GPT-4o’s image capabilities changed visual creativity.

entry.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics for physical-world control
entry.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics and Gemini Robotics-ER, extending Gemini 2.0 with vision-language-action control and embodied spatial reasoning for robots.

entry.title: Claude Code launches, becoming the first widely adopted production coding agent
entry.summary: Claude Code (2025) became the first widely adopted production-grade coding agent. How AI evolved from code assistant to autonomous programmer that plans, codes, and fixes bugs.

entry.title: OpenAI whistleblower Suchir Balaji's death is ruled a suicide, spotlighting AI safety culture
entry.summary: Suchir Balaji, an OpenAI whistleblower, was found dead in 2025 — ruled a suicide. The tragedy that sparked debate about AI safety culture and whistleblower protections in tech.

entry.title: EU AI Act takes effect, beginning the world's first comprehensive AI regulation enforcement
entry.summary: The EU AI Act took effect in 2025 — the world’s first comprehensive AI law entered enforcement. How Europe’s risk-based regulation reshaped how AI is built and deployed globally.

entry.title: 'Vibe coding' is coined, capturing a new paradigm of AI-assisted programming
entry.summary: ‘Vibe coding’ — coined by Andrej Karpathy in 2025 — captured the new paradigm where AI does the coding and humans guide with natural language. The term that defined a shift.

entry.title: OpenAI launches Operator, the first AI agent that can browse the web autonomously
entry.summary: OpenAI Operator (2025) was the first AI agent that could autonomously browse the web and complete tasks. How agentic AI moved from chatbots to action-taking digital assistants.

entry.title: DeepSeek releases R1, an open-source reasoning model that shocks global markets
entry.summary: DeepSeek R1: an open-source reasoning model matching OpenAI’s best at a fraction of the cost. How a Chinese AI lab shocked global markets in 2025.

entry.title: Google launches Gemini 2.0 with Project Mariner, unveiling a vision for AI agents
entry.summary: Google launched Gemini 2.0 with Project Mariner in December 2024 — an AI agent that could browse the web and control a browser. Google’s vision for AI agents.

entry.title: Anthropic introduces the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard connecting AI to real-world tools
entry.summary: MCP (Model Context Protocol) by Anthropic — an open standard connecting AI models to real-world tools and data. How a protocol could unify AI tool integration.

entry.title: AlphaFold developers win Nobel Prize in Chemistry, the first Nobel awarded for AI-driven scientific discovery
entry.summary: AlphaFold developers won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry — the first Nobel awarded for AI-driven scientific discovery. How AI transformed biology and earned science’s highest honor.

entry.title: OpenAI releases o1, the first reasoning model that 'thinks before it answers'
entry.summary: OpenAI o1 (September 2024) was the first reasoning model that ‘thought before answering.’ How inference-time compute improved AIME math scores from 13% to 83%.

entry.title: Meta releases Llama 3.1 405B, the first frontier-level open-source AI model
entry.summary: Llama 3.1 405B (July 2024) was the first open-weight AI model to reach frontier capabilities. Meta proved open models could match proprietary systems at scale.

entry.title: Major record labels sue AI music generators Suno and Udio for copyright infringement
entry.summary: Major record labels sued AI music generators Suno and Udio in 2024 for copyright infringement. The legal battle that could decide the future of AI-generated music.

entry.title: Anthropic releases Claude 3.5 Sonnet, setting a new standard for coding AI
entry.summary: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024) set a new standard for AI coding capabilities. Anthropic’s model became the developer favorite for programming tasks. Timeline and impact.

entry.title: NVIDIA becomes the world's most valuable company, a symbolic peak of AI-driven market dominance
entry.summary: NVIDIA became the world’s most valuable company in June 2024 — a symbolic milestone of AI-driven market dominance. Timeline of NVIDIA’s rise to the top.

entry.title: Apple announces Apple Intelligence at WWDC, bringing on-device AI to over a billion devices
entry.summary: Apple Intelligence announced at WWDC 2024 — bringing on-device AI to a billion devices. How Apple entered the AI race with privacy-focused, integrated AI capabilities.

entry.title: Scarlett Johansson challenges OpenAI over voice that sounds 'eerily similar' to hers
entry.summary: Scarlett Johansson challenged OpenAI in May 2024 over a ChatGPT voice that sounded ‘eerily similar’ to hers. The controversy over AI voice cloning and celebrity likeness rights.

entry.title: OpenAI releases GPT-4o, bringing real-time voice conversation to everyone
entry.summary: GPT-4o (May 2024) made real-time voice conversations with AI available to everyone. OpenAI’s omnimodal model combined text, vision, and audio in one neural network.

entry.title: EU approves the world's first comprehensive AI law
entry.summary: The EU AI Act became law in 2024 — the world’s first comprehensive AI regulation. How Europe’s risk-based framework set global standards for AI governance.

entry.title: Google releases Gemini 1.5 Pro with a million-token context window
entry.summary: Gemini 1.5 Pro (February 2024) introduced a 1 million token context window. Google’s most capable model could process entire books and codebases at once.

entry.title: OpenAI previews Sora, the first text-to-video model that looked like it was working
entry.summary: Sora: OpenAI’s February 2024 text-to-video model that stunned the world with realistic AI-generated videos. Timeline of how video generation entered the mainstream.

entry.title: Sam Altman fired and rehired in four days — the defining corporate governance crisis of the AI era
entry.summary: Sam Altman fired and rehired in 4 days (November 2023) — the defining corporate drama of the AI era. How a boardroom battle nearly collapsed OpenAI and changed AI governance.

entry.title: OpenAI holds first DevDay, unveiling GPT-4 Turbo, custom GPTs, and a platform strategy
entry.summary: OpenAI DevDay (November 2023) unveiled GPT-4 Turbo, custom GPTs, and the GPT Store. How one event reshaped the AI developer ecosystem and set OpenAI’s product direction.

entry.title: Auto-GPT goes viral, bringing autonomous AI agents to mainstream developers
entry.summary: Auto-GPT (March 2023) was the first autonomous AI agent to go viral. An open-source experiment that could set its own goals and execute tasks — sparking the AI agents movement.

entry.title: OpenAI releases GPT-4, the first multimodal large language model
entry.summary: GPT-4 release date: March 14, 2023. OpenAI’s first multimodal LLM scored top 10% on the bar exam and set a new AI capability baseline.

entry.title: Meta releases LLaMA, triggering the open-weight LLM revolution
entry.summary: Meta’s LLaMA (February 2023) was a set of open-weight foundation models that sparked the open-source LLM revolution. How leaked weights democratized access to large language models.

entry.title: Microsoft launches AI-powered Bing and the 'Sydney' chatbot captivates the world
entry.summary: Microsoft launched AI-powered Bing with the ‘Sydney’ chatbot in February 2023. How GPT-4-powered search threatened Google’s dominance and captivated the internet.

entry.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT, reaching 100 million users in two months
entry.summary: When did ChatGPT launch? Released November 30, 2022, it reached 100 million users in 60 days — the fastest-growing app in history. Timeline, impact, and key milestones.

entry.title: Character.AI launches and pioneers the AI companion phenomenon
entry.summary: Character.AI launched in 2022 — the platform that let you chat with anyone, real or fictional. How AI companions became a phenomenon and sparked debates about AI relationships.

entry.title: Stable Diffusion open-sources text-to-image generation to the public
entry.summary: Stable Diffusion: the open-source AI image generator released in August 2022 that democratized text-to-image. How a free model changed the AI art landscape forever.

entry.title: GitHub Copilot launches generally, putting AI pair programming in every major IDE
entry.summary: GitHub Copilot launched in June 2022, putting AI pair programming in every developer’s IDE. How OpenAI Codex changed software development and the meaning of coding.

entry.title: OpenAI releases DALL-E 2 and brings AI-generated images to the mainstream
entry.summary: DALL-E 2 launch: OpenAI’s April 2022 image generator that brought AI art to the mainstream. How text-to-image changed creativity, copyright, and the internet.

entry.title: European Commission proposes the first comprehensive AI regulation framework
entry.summary: The EU AI Act proposal (April 2021) — the world’s first comprehensive AI regulation. How Europe proposed a risk-based framework for governing AI that reshaped global tech policy.

entry.title: OpenAI unveils DALL-E, demonstrating text-to-image generation for the first time
entry.summary: DALL-E (January 2021): OpenAI’s 12-billion-parameter model that could generate images from text descriptions. The first glimpse of AI’s creative potential in visual art.

entry.title: DeepMind's AlphaFold solves protein folding — a 50-year grand challenge in biology
entry.summary: AlphaFold: DeepMind solved the 50-year protein folding challenge in 2020. How AI predicted protein structures with atomic accuracy, transforming biology and medicine.

entry.title: OpenAI releases GPT-3, demonstrating that scaling language models unlocks emergent capabilities
entry.summary: GPT-3 (175 billion parameters) showed scaling unlocks emergent AI capabilities. How OpenAI’s 2020 paper validated the scaling hypothesis and changed AI.

entry.title: OpenAI says GPT-2 is 'too dangerous to release' — the first mainstream AI safety debate goes global
entry.summary: OpenAI said GPT-2 was “too dangerous to release” in 2019 — the first mainstream AI safety debate. How a language model sparked global conversation about responsible AI.

entry.title: Google releases BERT and transforms NLP with bidirectional pre-training
entry.summary: BERT: Google’s 2018 breakthrough that revolutionized NLP with bidirectional pre-training. How BERT achieved SOTA on 11 benchmarks and became the foundation of modern language AI.

entry.title: "Attention Is All You Need" — the Transformer architecture is born
entry.summary: Attention Is All You Need: the 2017 paper that introduced the Transformer. Cited 250K+ times, it founded GPT, BERT, AlphaFold, and all modern AI.

entry.title: Microsoft's Tay chatbot becomes racist in 16 hours — the first viral AI safety meltdown
entry.summary: Microsoft Tay (2016) became racist in 16 hours — the first viral AI safety incident. How a chatbot revealed the dangers of learning from unfiltered public data.

entry.title: AlphaGo defeats Lee Sedol, a milestone once believed decades away
entry.summary: AlphaGo vs Lee Sedol: DeepMind’s AI defeated a Go world champion years before experts predicted. The 200 million viewer match that changed AI perception.

entry.title: ResNet wins ImageNet — residual connections enable ultra-deep networks
entry.summary: ResNet (2015) won ImageNet with residual connections that enabled 152-layer networks. How skip connections solved the degradation problem and enabled deep learning at scale.

entry.title: Google open-sources TensorFlow — deep learning becomes accessible
entry.summary: TensorFlow (2015): Google open-sourced the deep learning framework that became the industry standard. How open-sourcing AI infrastructure accelerated research and adoption worldwide.

entry.title: Attention mechanism proposed — the foundation of modern AI architectures
entry.summary: The attention mechanism (2014) — Bahdanau, Cho, and Bengio’s breakthrough that enabled Transformer and all modern AI. How a simple idea changed machine translation forever.

entry.title: Ian Goodfellow invents Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)
entry.summary: GANs (2014): Ian Goodfellow’s Generative Adversarial Networks that pitted two neural networks against each other. How adversarial training changed AI’s ability to generate realistic data.

entry.title: Google acquires DeepMind and ignites the AI talent race
entry.summary: Google acquires DeepMind in 2014 for £400M — the deal that started the AI talent race. How one acquisition concentrated world-leading AI talent inside a single company.

entry.title: DeepMind shows DQN playing Atari games from raw pixels — deep reinforcement learning's first breakthrough
entry.summary: DeepMind’s DQN (2013) played Atari games from raw pixels using deep reinforcement learning. The first time AI learned to play games the way humans do — just from seeing the screen.

entry.title: AlexNet wins ImageNet and ignites the deep learning revolution
entry.summary: AlexNet wins ImageNet 2012 — the breakthrough that sparked the deep learning revolution. How Krizhevsky, Sutskever, and Hinton’s convolutional network changed AI forever.

entry.title: Siri launches on iPhone 4S — millions of ordinary people meet AI for the first time
entry.summary: Siri launched on iPhone 4S in 2011 — the first time millions of ordinary people used conversational AI. How Apple brought AI assistants into everyday life.

entry.title: IBM Watson defeats human champions on Jeopardy!
entry.summary: IBM Watson defeats Jeopardy! champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter in 2011. How a question-answering AI system proved machines could understand natural language.

entry.title: IBM Deep Blue defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov
entry.summary: Deep Blue vs Kasparov 1997: IBM’s supercomputer defeated the world chess champion in a match that proved machines could outthink humans. A landmark in AI history.

entry.title: Second AI Winter — expert systems market collapses
entry.summary: The Second AI Winter (1987) — the expert systems market collapsed after a decade of hype. Learn what caused the crash, how it reshaped AI research, and the lessons for today.

entry.title: Joseph Weizenbaum creates ELIZA, the first conversational agent in history
entry.summary: ELIZA (1966): Joseph Weizenbaum’s chatbot that simulated a psychotherapist. The first conversational AI — people formed emotional attachments to it. Timeline and legacy.

entry.title: Frank Rosenblatt demonstrates the Perceptron, the first artificial neural network that learns
entry.summary: Frank Rosenblatt’s Perceptron (1958) — the first artificial neural network that could learn. Learn how it worked, why it caused excitement, and how it led to today’s deep learning.

entry.title: Dartmouth Summer Research Project: Artificial Intelligence is formally founded
entry.summary: The 1956 Dartmouth Summer Research Project where John McCarthy coined ‘Artificial Intelligence.’ The eight-week workshop that birthed AI as a field. Full history and legacy.

entry.title: Alan Turing publishes "Computing Machinery and Intelligence", proposing what becomes the Turing Test
entry.summary: Alan Turing’s 1950 paper proposed the Imitation Game — the first test for machine intelligence. How a simple question started the field of AI.
